feedback: Iteration 0 has no race data, so this review rests only on the public contract and the baseline's own contents. The candidate is valid: all sensor positions and weights are inside their limits, base_speed 1.6 and kp 2.0 are in range, and line_loss 'last_direction' is an allowed option. Its sign convention is consistent with the contract: sensors at negative x carry negative weights, so a line on the left gives a positive signal, which steers left. Nothing in it looks obviously broken, and no earlier race exists to show it is worse than anything else, so the bar is validity. Approve it so the first race produces telemetry. Nothing here predicts how it will perform. When the race reports back, use the measurements to choose the next change. If rms_error or max_error is large, or line_loss_events is above zero, reduce base_speed or raise kp and kd. If steering_oscillation is high, raise kd before raising kp. If completion_time is well under 3 s with a clean track, raise base_speed. If the run stalls or goes off track on the slalom, lower kp and check that the sensor_size and sensor spacing cover the 25 mm tape.
requested_changes: If the race shows high steering_oscillation, increase kd from 0.1 toward 0.3 and keep kp at 2.0, because kd is the only damping term in the baseline.

If the race shows line_loss_events above zero or max_error near 0.06 m, reduce base_speed from 1.6 toward 1.2 before changing any gains, because the slalom is the most likely place for the line to be lost.
If the race completes with low max_error and completion_time well under 3 s, raise base_speed in steps of 0.2 while keeping the same gains, to find the speed limit before tracking fails.
